facts.fact: The paper states that data entry is done at the health office, which prints the birth or death registration certificate once entry is complete, that the offices are linked online to a central database over a secured GPRS/3G mobile network, and that registration is completed within 15 minutes against one month on paper; the system dates from 2017.
facts.system: Egyptian Birth and Death Registration System (EBDRS)

facts.fact: The paper states that EBDRS was developed and implemented in 2017 to automate 4,571 health offices, 300 health departments and 27 health directorates and link them to a central database, by the account of the Ministry of Planning, Monitoring and Administrative Reform; it gives no total number of health offices against the 4,571.
facts.system: Egyptian Birth and Death Registration System (EBDRS)

facts.fact: The paper states that the Ministry of Planning, Monitoring and Administrative Reform developed and implemented EBDRS in 2017 in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, in whose system the registration is held, under the existing Civil Registration Act with no change in the law.
facts.system: Egyptian Birth and Death Registration System (EBDRS)

facts.fact: Law 143 of 1994, issued on 7 June 1994, gives the Civil Status Organization of the Ministry of Interior the execution of the law and the registration of births and deaths in the event registers, which Article 3 defines as paper or automated records held on computer, with health offices under the health ministry receiving and entering the notifications and sending them weekly to the civil registry sections.
facts.system: Civil status event registers of the Civil Status Organization

facts.fact: Article 18 of Law 143 of 1994 creates a special fund at the Ministry of Interior, fed first by sums the State allots it in the general budget and also by the Organization's fees, grants, loans and fines, to pay for information centres, automated issuing stations, new civil registry sections and units, equipment and running costs.
facts.system: Civil status event registers of the Civil Status Organization

facts.fact: The article reports a letter from the head of the health ministry's preventive medicine and public health sector that refers to an automated system for registering births and deaths at the health offices, onto which data are entered; the article states no date for the letter, so its published date is used.
facts.system: automated system for registering births and deaths at health offices

facts.fact: The head of the Ministry of Health and Population's preventive medicine and public health sector wrote to every health affairs directorate in the country about the data entered on the automated births and deaths registration system at the health offices, and health inspectors at those offices issue the burial permits and death certificates; the article states no date for the letter, so its published date is used.
facts.system: automated system for registering births and deaths at health offices

facts.fact: The health ministry's preventive medicine sector instructed all health affairs directorates to unify and improve the quality of data entered on the automated births and deaths registration system at health offices, requiring every hospital, public, private and university, to use only the unified death notification form (January 2021 version, with a QR code) and health inspectors to accept it, with legal action for any laxity; the letter cites earlier instructions of October 2024, and the article states no date for it, so its published date is used.
facts.system: automated system for registering births and deaths at health offices
